subject: Re: Compensation proposal after May 30th throughput regression — credit amount & trial extension
messages:
From: Avery Morales <avery@luxelabs.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan@luxelabs.ai>, Luxe Labs Support <ops@luxelabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput drop on May 30th — request for remediation and credit

Hi Diego,

We saw a sustained throughput degradation across our production inference pool starting ~09:10 UTC on May 30th that lasted roughly 42 minutes. Our customer-facing SLAs include a throughput & latency target tied to their subscription, and this regression impacted three paying customers. Ops flagged a spike in 429s and elevated tail latency.

Can Redwood provide a clear remediation plan and propose compensation for the impacted windows? Specifically:
- A credit estimate we can present to our customers (token-based or dollar equivalent)
- A short-term trial extension or promo to help placate churn risk for two affected teams

We appreciate the prompt support during the incident; we just need the commercial follow-through.

Thanks,
Avery
Director of Platform, Luxe Labs

On behalf of the Luxe platform team
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Avery Morales <avery@luxelabs.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput drop on May 30th — request for remediation and credit

Hi Avery — thanks for raising this and for the clear summary. I'm sorry Luxe hit this regression; we know how sensitive production customers are to any hit in throughput.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- Engineering is validating the root cause (initial signal indicates a routing imbalance during a GPU rebalancing job). We'll send a concise postmortem tomorrow with logs and mitigation.
- Commercially, we can offer: a token credit equivalent for the affected window (we're modelling both token and USD), and a 30-day extension of the Luxe Labs trial promo for the two at-risk teams.
- I'll run the proposed numbers by Sean (finance) and Monica (CS escalation lead) and circle back by EOD tomorrow.

Would Luxe prefer a straightforward token credit (tokens at list redemption rate) or a flat USD credit? Either works, but we want to align on what your customers prefer to see on invoices.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Compensation numbers for Luxe Labs (draft)

Diego / Monica —

I've reviewed usage for Luxe during the 09:10–09:52 UTC window. Attached is a quick workbook with per-customer token counts and a suggested credit policy: 1) 100% token refund for failed requests (429s/errors), 2) 40% credit on elevated tail latency requests (p90+ > baseline) and 3) a separate goodwill pool of $1,500 applied as account-level credit for churn mitigation.

We can convert tokens to USD at the public list rate or apply a direct dollar credit. I'd recommend the combined approach (token refund + $1.5k goodwill) so Luxe can present immediate relief and a line-item that looks like vendor accountability.

If Luxe wants to escalate the dollar amount, we can consider a one-time trial extension up to 60 days for the two teams, rather than the 30-day default.

Sean
VP, Revenue Operations

Attachment: proposed_credit-summary.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Avery Morales <avery@luxelabs.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Throughput drop on May 30th — request for remediation and credit

Avery —

Thanks for your patience. Sean and I discussed options and here's what we propose to resolve quickly:

1) Credit: token-based refund for all requests that returned 429 or 5xx during 09:10–09:52 UTC, converted to account credit at list rate.
2) Goodwill: $1,500 account credit to Luxe Labs to apply towards any invoice.
3) Trial extension: 45-day extension of the current promo for the two teams identified by Jordan; this gives them runway while we finish the postmortem.
4) Postmortem: we'll deliver a formal postmortem by EOD Wed (Jun 2) with corrective actions and a timeline for the rebalancing guardrail.

If that package works for Luxe, we'll prepare a short amendment and a DocuSign link for acceptance. If you'd rather a flat USD amount in lieu of tokens, tell us what you'll need and we'll reprice.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Escalations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: billing_history_may.csv
From: Avery Morales <avery@luxelabs.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan@luxelabs.ai>, Luxe Labs Support <ops@luxelabs.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compensation proposal after May 30th throughput regression — credit amount & trial extension

Monica / Diego / Sean —

Thank you — that package looks reasonable and will be straightforward to present to our Finance and Ops committees. A couple quick asks before we sign:

- Can you include the per-customer token counts (so we can show individual impacted teams) in the amendment?
- For the 45-day extension, can you include language that it applies only to workloads provisioned in our existing Dedicated pool (to avoid folks trying unrelated usage)?
- Please send the postmortem as promised; our ops team will need the mitigation timeline for their runbooks.

If you send the amendment + DocuSign, I'll route it internally and aim to sign by EOD Friday. We appreciate the rapid turnaround.

Best,
Avery
Director of Platform, Luxe Labs

Attachments referenced: luxe_postmortem-draft.pdf (will accept final PM), proposed_credit-summary.xlsx (for CFO review)
